summary: Untouched, the port draws the same static N-band segment display with identical per-segment hues, but its brightness parity is inverted and — decisively for a pattern whose entire point is per-segment control — 6 of its 8 dials are completely dead where the original's are live.
observations: Both sides are STATIC after startup: a fade-in from black over ~2 s, then a frozen image. survey (60 s @ 5 fps) shows zeroMotionFrames 291/300 on BOTH sides and brightnessTrend steady; ms-late (--skip 120 --seconds 20 @ 20 fps) confirms the exact same frame at t=120/130/139 s on both. Seed 7 renders identically to seed 1 (meanBrightness 72.5 orig / 83.5 port vs 74.2 / 84.7) — no randomness on either side.

Untouched steady state, 60 px strip, exact --dump values at t=3 s: orig = px0-14 [50,0,0], px15-29 [127,255,0], px30-44 [0,50,50], px45-59 [127,0,255]. port = px0-14 [255,0,0], px15-29 [44,89,0], px30-44 [0,255,255], px45-59 [44,0,89]. Segment boundaries and HUES match exactly (h = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75); only the per-segment VALUE differs.

Brightness parity is INVERTED. The original renders even-indexed segments dim and odd-indexed segments at full value; the port does the opposite (segment 0 full, segment 1 dim). Verified at every segment count: at Segments=1.0 (12 segments) orig = dim,full,dim,full,... starting dim, port = full,dim,full,dim,... starting full, with the 12 hues (i/12) identical index-for-index on both sides.

The dim level itself differs: original dim segments render at value 50/255 (~0.196), the port's at 89/255 (~0.349) — the port's 'off/dim' segments are ~1.8x too bright. This is why the port's whole-strip meanBrightness sits at 84.7 vs the original's 74.2 (+14%).

Startup transient differs in shape though not in total length. Normalised to each side's final value, the original crosses 50% at ~1.35 s and saturates at ~2.1 s; the port crosses 50% at ~0.85 s and is at 95% by 1.5 s, saturating ~2.0 s. Both start from exact black (t=0, 0.05, 0.1 are all [0,0,0] on both sides). Port's fade-in is visibly the faster/front-loaded curve.

CONTROL-SURFACE MISMATCH: both sides expose 8 controls with matching kinds and order, but 4 of the 8 NAMES differ. orig: sliderActiveSegment, sliderState, sliderEffect, sliderSpeed, sliderSize, hsvPickerColor, sliderSegments, sliderEnableWebUI. port: sliderActiveZone, sliderZoneOnOff, sliderEffect, sliderSpeed, sliderZoneSize, hsvPickerColor, sliderZoneCount, sliderEnableWebUI. The port renamed the 'Segment' vocabulary to 'Zone', which changes the user-visible labels (ActiveSegment->ActiveZone, State->ZoneOnOff, Size->ZoneSize, Segments->ZoneCount).

probe (6 s window, --skip 3): orig has FIVE responsive dials (sliderState 4.17, sliderEffect 6.25, sliderSize 85.24, hsvPickerColor 22.25, sliderSegments 75.22); port has exactly ONE (sliderZoneCount 113.75). ActiveSegment/ActiveZone, Speed and EnableWebUI probe inert on both — ActiveSegment is a selector so a solo sweep legitimately shows nothing.

Manual multi-event sweeps confirm the probe's inerts on the port are REAL, not false inerts. sliderZoneOnOff swept at 11 points 0..1 (ms-st-*, 5 s windows, dumped at t=4): byte-identical output at every value. sliderZoneSize at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1: identical. hsvPickerColor at (0,1,1),(0.33,1,1),(0.66,1,1),(0,0,1): identical. sliderEffect at 0/0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8/1 over 12 s windows: identical. sliderActiveZone at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 (with Color pinned to white to give it something to select): identical.

Setter-interaction was ruled out on the port: sliderEffect=0.6 was re-run with sliderEnableWebUI=1, with sliderActiveZone=0, with sliderActiveZone=0.5, with sliderEnableWebUI=0, and with the full combo EnableWebUI=1 + ActiveZone=0 + ZoneOnOff=1 — all five produced the identical static 255/0/0 | 44/89/0 | 0/255/255 | 44/0/89 frame at t=4, 6, 8 and 11 s. No combination of port dials makes it animate or change.

The original by contrast is a working segment editor. sliderActiveSegment selects which band the other dials act on: with hsvPickerColor=0,0,1 (white), ActiveSegment 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1 whitens px0-14 / px15-29 / px30-44 / px45-59 / px45-59 respectively.

Original sliderSize resizes the active segment and pushes the rest along: at Size=0.25 seg0 is 14 px (0-13), at 0.5 it is 29 px (0-28), at 0.75 44 px (0-43), at 1.0 59 px (0-58) with the remaining segments squeezed into the tail. Port's sliderZoneSize leaves the four 15-px bands untouched at every value.

Original sliderEffect animates the active segment: Effect=0 solid dim red; 0.2 and 0.4 fade the segment to black within ~1 s and re-pulse it faintly (px7 reads 3,0,0 at t=4 then 0,0,0 by t=5, back to 2,0,0 by t=11); 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0 run a continuous hue cycle on that segment (e.g. Effect=1: 50/40/0 -> 0/50/40 -> 40/0/50 across 0.5-1 s steps), capped at the segment's 50/255 value. Only the active segment animates; the other three stay frozen. Port shows zero animation at any Effect value.

Original sliderSpeed is only meaningful with an animating Effect, and it does work: with Effect=1, Speed=1 gives a tight ~1.5 s hue cycle on segment 0 (values repeat as 50/40/0, 0/50/40, 40/0/50 at 1 s spacing), Speed=0/0.25/0.5/0.75 give visibly slower, non-repeating-at-that-spacing walks. Port: constant 255/0/0 at every Speed with Effect=1.

Original sliderState is a genuine on/off toggle but with a quirk: at exactly 0 and exactly 1 the active segment keeps its default dim 50 value, and at every intermediate value tested (0.1 through 0.9) the segment goes fully black [0,0,0]. Port's sliderZoneOnOff does nothing at any of those 11 values.

Segments / ZoneCount is the one dial that works on both, but the value->count mapping is off by one over most of the range. A 21-point sweep (0 to 1 in 0.05) gives orig = floor(1 + 11*v) and port = floor(1 + 12*v) capped at 12. They agree at v = 0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.55, 0.65, 1.00 and differ by exactly one segment at the other 11 points (e.g. v=0.5: orig 6 segments, port 7; v=0.95: orig 11, port 12).

Segment layout under ZoneCount otherwise matches: both divide 60 px into equal runs with the remainder going to the last segment (e.g. at 7 segments orig runs are 8,8,8,8,8,8,12 px), and both assign hue = index/count. Only the count mapping and the dim/full parity differ.
Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both); no compile or runtime errors on either side; no harness warnings on any run.

dials.name: ActiveSegment (orig) / ActiveZone (port)
dials.origEffect: Selects which segment the Color/Size/Effect/State dials act on. With Color pinned to white, values 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 whiten segments 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 respectively; 1.0 also selects the last segment.
dials.portEffect: INERT. No change at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1, alone or combined with Color, Effect, ZoneOnOff or EnableWebUI. Also renamed from ActiveSegment to ActiveZone.

dials.name: State (orig) / ZoneOnOff (port)
dials.origEffect: Toggles the active segment. Exactly 0 or exactly 1 leaves it at its default dim value (50/255); any intermediate value (0.1-0.9 tested) blanks it to [0,0,0].
dials.portEffect: INERT across 11 values 0..1 on a 5 s window and across 10 s windows — byte-identical output. Also renamed from State to ZoneOnOff.

dials.name: Effect
dials.origEffect: Picks the active segment's animation: 0 = solid; 0.2/0.4 = fade-out then faint re-pulse; 0.6/0.8/1.0 = continuous hue cycling on that segment only, amplitude capped at the segment's own value. Non-active segments never animate.
dials.portEffect: INERT at 0/0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8/1 over 12 s windows, and inert in every combination with ActiveZone / ZoneOnOff / EnableWebUI. The port never animates at all after its 2 s fade-in.

dials.name: Speed
dials.origEffect: Sets the rate of whatever Effect is running on the active segment. With Effect=1, Speed=1 cycles the hue about once per 1.5 s; lower Speed values slow it proportionally. Inert on its own (Effect=0 is a static effect), which is why the probe called it inert.
dials.portEffect: INERT at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 with Effect=1 — segment 0 holds 255/0/0 from t=5 to t=19 at every value.

dials.name: Size (orig) / ZoneSize (port)
dials.origEffect: Resizes the active segment, pushing the others down the strip: 14 px at 0.25, 29 px at 0.5, 44 px at 0.75, 59 px at 1.0 (remaining segments squeezed to 1 px each at the tail).
dials.portEffect: INERT at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 — four 15-px bands at every value. Also renamed from Size to ZoneSize.

dials.name: Color (hsvPickerColor)
dials.origEffect: Sets the active segment's colour AND promotes it to full value: (0,1,1) makes seg0 [255,0,0] (vs its default dim [50,0,0]), (0.33,1,1) [5,255,0], (0.66,1,1) [0,10,255], (0,0,1) [255,255,255]. Other segments unaffected.
dials.portEffect: INERT at all four test colours including full white — output unchanged from untouched.

dials.name: Segments (orig) / ZoneCount (port)
dials.origEffect: Sets the number of equal segments as floor(1 + 11*v), 1 to 12. Hue of segment i is i/count; even-indexed segments dim (value 50/255), odd-indexed full.
dials.portEffect: WORKS, but as floor(1 + 12*v) capped at 12 — one segment more than the original over 11 of 21 sweep points. Same equal-division layout and same i/count hues, but the dim/full parity is inverted (even segments full, odd dim) and the dim level is 89/255 instead of 50/255. Also renamed from Segments to ZoneCount.

dials.name: EnableWebUI
dials.origEffect: Dial effect unverifiable from output — probe delta 0.00, and a manual 0/1 check changes nothing. It presumably only gates the pattern's web UI, which the harness does not render.
dials.portEffect: Same — no output effect at 0 or 1, alone or combined with Effect. Name and kind match the original.

feedback: The port's biggest gap is that only ZoneCount is wired up. ActiveZone, ZoneOnOff, Effect, Speed, ZoneSize and Color are all completely inert — verified byte-identical output across full sweeps and across five multi-control combinations. For a pattern called 'Multisegment Demo' the per-segment editing is the pattern; restoring those six dials is the whole fix.

Restore the per-segment selection model: an ActiveSegment slider that maps its 0..1 range onto the current segment index, with State / Effect / Size / Color applying ONLY to that one segment and leaving the others frozen. In the original, setting Color on segment 2 leaves segments 0, 1 and 3 pixel-for-pixel unchanged.

Restore per-segment animation. The original's Effect dial gives the active segment a solid look at 0, a fade-to-black-then-repulse at ~0.2-0.4, and a continuous hue cycle at ~0.6-1.0, with Speed setting the cycle rate (Effect=1, Speed=1 is roughly a 1.5 s hue loop). The port is completely static after startup at every dial setting — it never animates a single pixel.
Fix the segment brightness parity: the original renders even-indexed segments DIM and odd-indexed segments at FULL value; the port has it exactly backwards. Verified at 1, 4 and 12 segments.

Fix the dim/off level: the original's non-active segments render at value 50/255 (~0.196), the port's at 89/255 (~0.349). Dropping the port's dim level to ~0.196 also fixes the +14% whole-strip mean brightness offset (84.7 vs 74.2).

Fix the segment-count mapping off-by-one: the original computes floor(1 + 11*v) (so v=0.5 gives 6 segments, v=0.95 gives 11), the port computes floor(1 + 12*v) capped at 12 (7 and 12 at the same values). They only agree at v = 0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.55, 0.65 and 1.00.

Rename the four diverging controls back to the original's vocabulary — sliderActiveSegment, sliderState, sliderSize, sliderSegments (currently sliderActiveZone, sliderZoneOnOff, sliderZoneSize, sliderZoneCount). Kinds and ordering already match; only the user-visible labels are wrong.

Match the original's State semantics if you restore it: exactly 0 and exactly 1 leave the active segment at its normal dim value, while every intermediate value blanks it to pure black. That is an odd contract but it is what the original does across 0.1-0.9.

Minor: soften the startup fade. Both sides fade in from black and saturate at ~2.0-2.1 s, but the port front-loads it (50% by ~0.85 s) where the original is slower through the middle (50% by ~1.35 s). Low priority next to the dead dials.
Do NOT chase segment boundaries or hues — those already match exactly. Boundaries are identical at every segment count tested, and hue = index/count agrees index-for-index at 1, 4 and 12 segments.
